journey.title: Tab out of the visit date into the access notes
journey.goal: Pressing Tab in the open date field moves focus to the next form field so the user can keep typing

functionalJourney.title: Pick a visit date with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a day in the calendar fills the visit date field

guards.title: Pick the next day with arrow keys
guards.goal: Arrow keys move the calendar focus and Enter commits the date

plan.root_cause: The datepicker's keydown listener on the input field prevents the default Tab key behavior, trapping focus inside the datepicker popup and preventing movement to the next form field.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the datepicker's keydown listener to allow the Tab key to bubble up and trigger the browser's default focus traversal, while preserving all other key handling for datepicker navigation.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab while the datepicker is open will move focus to the next focusable element in the tab order (the Access notes input), enabling keyboard-only users to navigate the form without mouse interaction.
functional_risks: The datepicker may lose internal keyboard navigation if the Tab key was previously used for popup navigation (though unlikely given arrow key usage).
Shift+Tab behavior is not explicitly addressed but will follow the same pattern as Tab due to the key check.

If the datepicker relies on Tab for internal popup navigation (e.g., moving between grid cells), this could break that functionality. However, the observed datepicker uses arrow keys for navigation, making this risk low.
verification_requirements: Tab key moves focus from visit-date input to notes input when datepicker is open.
Shift+Tab moves focus from notes input to visit-date input when datepicker is open.
Arrow right and Enter keys still function to change the date (regression guard).
Datepicker remains operable via arrow keys, Enter, and Escape for date selection and dismissal.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker's keydown listener on the input field prevents the default Tab key behavior, and the datepicker popup's buttons are in the natural tab order, trapping focus inside the popup when Tab is pressed.
plan.repair_strategy: 1) Modify the input field's keydown listener to allow Tab (and Shift+Tab) to bubble up for default browser focus traversal. 2) Make the datepicker popup's focusable buttons (prev, next, view switch, today, clear) non-focusable via Tab by setting tabindex=-1 when the popup is shown, and restore on hide.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab while the datepicker is open will move focus to the next focusable element in the tab order (the Access notes input), enabling keyboard-only users to navigate the form without mouse interaction. Shift+Tab will move focus to the previous element.
functional_risks: The datepicker popup buttons will no longer be reachable via Tab, but they remain operable via arrow keys, Enter, and Escape as per the datepicker's design.

If the datepicker is used in inline mode (without an input field), the buttons will still be in the tab order because the show/hide methods are not called. This is acceptable because inline pickers are part of the page's tab order.
The tabindex manipulation could conflict with other scripts that manage tabindex on the same buttons, but the datepicker controls its own buttons.
verification_requirements: Tab key moves focus from visit-date input to notes input when datepicker is open.
Shift+Tab moves focus from notes input to visit-date input when datepicker is open.
Arrow right and Enter keys still function to change the date (regression guard).
Datepicker remains operable via arrow keys, Enter, and Escape for date selection and dismissal.
The prev/next buttons, view switch, today, and clear buttons are not focusable via Tab when the picker is open.
